videos.title: The Space Force Showed Us Its Weapons Used in Iran and Venezuela | WSJ Equipped
videos.description:
An array of U.S. Space Force electromagnetic warfare systems are playing a key role in protecting American troops and degrading enemy satellites around the world. 

The Journal was granted rare access to a Space Force base in Colorado to learn how those systems work, and to speak exclusively with Guardians who flew them overseas to support operations in both Venezuela and Iran.

Hours after Tech. Sgt. Joshua Lomax jammed satellites to create a protective bubble around U.S. forces capturing Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro, he was given 72 hours to pack up his equipment and head to the Middle East, where the U.S. would soon launch its war against Iran.

videos.title: India's Mittal Says His Satellite Venture Is Ahead of Musk's Starlink
videos.description:
India's foreign minister said the growing calls for “middle powers” to play a more active role in the world requires them to find partners who can cooperate in the areas that matter. External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar said these countries “need to be more active, need to deal more with each other, and figure out a way of moving the needle on issues of interest to them.” 

Indian tycoon Sunil Bharti Mittal said his Eutelsat OneWeb venture is “significantly ahead” of Starlink in India’s satellite-communication approval queue, amid Elon Musk’s criticism that some oligarchs are blocking his attempts to gain spectrum access in the country.

Bloomberg's The Pulse With Francine Lacqua presented special programming from New Delhi, discussing the global outlook and India's role as one of the fastest-growing major economies. 

Today's guests: Helene Budliger Artieda, Switzerland's State Secretary for Economic Affairs; Kevin Sneader, Goldman Sachs President of Asia Pacific Ex-Japan

videos.title: Unlocking Investment Opportunities in Emerging Markets to Create Jobs | 2026 Annual Meetings
videos.description:
How can private capital mobilization unlock investment, support businesses, and create more and better jobs in emerging markets and developing economies?

Watch Unlocking Investment Opportunities in Emerging Markets to Create Jobs from the 2026 World Bank Group-IMF Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

World Bank Group President Ajay Banga joined investors, regulators, development finance leaders, and private sector partners to explore how to mobilize private investment at scale. The discussion focused on building investable project pipelines, using guarantees and other tools to share risk, expanding local-currency financing, strengthening domestic capital markets, and creating investment models that can be replicated across projects and markets.

Drawing on examples from infrastructure, energy, and small business financing, speakers explored how governments, development institutions, and the private sector can work together to connect capital with opportunity and support job creation.

SPEAKERS
• Ajay Banga — President, World Bank Group
 • Shriti Vadera — Chair, Private Sector Investment Lab 
 • Shemara Wikramanayake — Managing Director and CEO, Macquarie Group @macquarie 
 • Michael Wehrle — Chief Executive Officer, BlueOrchard 
 • Basma Bentaher — Chief Development Officer, AMEA Power @AMEAPower 
 • Atsi Sheth — Chief Credit Officer, Moody’s Ratings
 • Ed Miliband — Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs
 • Jean-Paul Servais — Chair, Belgian FSMA; Chair, IOSCO
 • Ashishkumar Chauhan — Managing Director and CEO, National Stock Exchange of India (NSE)
 • Faheen Allibhoy — Managing Director, Global Head of Development Finance & Advisory, J.P. Morgan 
HOST & MODERATOR
• Sharanjit Leyl — Former BBC World News and Bloomberg TV anchor for Asia
 • Douglas Peterson — Former President and CEO, S&P Global

The 2026 Annual Meetings bring global leaders together in Bangkok, October 12–18, to discuss jobs, investment, growth, and practical solutions for development.

videos.description:

videos.title: Why This Deep Red State Is a Battleground for the GOP’s Future | WSJ
videos.description:
Idaho, deeply Republican and mostly rural, is about the furthest you could get from a battleground state. So it is no surprise it is often overlooked in the national media during midterm elections.

But under the surface there is a groundswell of tensions between traditional Republicans, the MAGA loyalists and newer hardline-right politicians tussling for power and influence in Idaho. This Mountain West state has become a key bellwether for the fight over what a post-Trump Republican Party could become at the national level, as well as a test lab for some of the nation’s most controversial conservative legislation.

WSJ’s Robbie Gramer returns to his home state of Idaho to explore what the tensions between Idaho’s traditional Republicans and a newer, hard-line political right could mean for the Republican party’s national identity ahead of the midterms.

videos.title: Why It's So Expensive To Run An Auto Repair Shop
videos.description:
Auto repair prices have risen far faster than overall inflation. Mechanics say one key reason is the new software, parts, and safety technology. Shops are spending more on software access and safety calibration equipment. While the number of auto repair shops has grown, some who work in the business say it is getting harder to keep up, especially for smaller ones.

videos.title: Inside Man: How Chinese Spies Used Lies, Romance And Betrayal To Target The Federal Reserve
videos.description:
One week after a friendly summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, CNBC details an aggressive plot by China to infiltrate one of the United States’ most important institutions: the Federal Reserve. This explosive documentary delves into the incredible saga of a Chinese spy's effort to obtain secrets from the inner confines of the U.S.' top bank. It's a tale of sex, money, deceit and betrayal that put some of the country’s vital economic and financial secrets at risk. With exclusive access to new documents, audio, photos and text messages, CNBC's Senior Washington Correspondent Eamon Javers uncovers the story of former Fed economist John Rogers and a Chinese spy posing as an economics student who he befriended in 2013. “Inside Man” is a spy story at the heart of the competition for global economic dominance, posing the question of whether Rogers was a spy himself or an unwitting dupe.
